title: Edge operator attestation playbook	6 approval experiments (WIP)
content:
Overview:
This working runbook outlines a set of small, measurable approval gate experiments for operator attestation during customer-managed networking handoffs in Private deployments. The goal is to produce signed, tamper-evident artifacts for each operator action while testing lightweight automation that lowers friction for routine changes.

Context / motivation:
- Many existing PRDs specify immutable logs and network gating but are quiet on the operator UX and experimental heuristics to safely auto-approve low-risk changes.
- Security teams require clear chain-of-custody artifacts for audits; product teams need fewer blocking approvals for routine ops.

Scope (in): customer VPC handoffs, operator-initiated config edits on customer-managed edge adapters, compact attestation artifacts, approval-state machine metadata, and small automation heuristics.
Scope (out): deep packet/firewall semantics, low-level KMS/HSM design (see KMS integration PRD), full eDiscovery tooling.

Goals:
- Emit a compact, signed attestation artifact for every operator-approved change that customers can ingest into SIEMs.
- Reduce median approval latency for routine ops by ~30% during experiments while keeping evidence suitable for SOC/ISO audits.
- Validate safety heuristics that allow safe auto-approve in well-defined scenarios.

Attestation artifact (compact canonical):
- artifact_id: art_<short-iso>_<id>
- tenant: tenant_id
- subject: customer_id
- change_summary: short free-text summary (operator)
- diff_digest: sha256(canonical-diff)
- operator: display_name + operator_id
- operator_assertion: checklist selections and free-text justification (20-200 chars)
- signature: base64(signature(operator_key, artifact_payload))
- control_plane_refs: list of request/event ids (comma separated)
- time_utc: iso8601
- approval_state: requested | human_approved | auto_approved | rejected | rolled_back
- governance_tags: free list (e.g., pci, gdpr, pilot-opt-in)

Rationale for compact artifact:
- Compact artifacts (~1-3 KB) are cheap to store and easy for customers to consume. Full diffs remain in encrypted blobstore behind signed URLs referenced by artifact. Auditors can validate digest/signature chain without needing full payload by default.

Minimal operator checklist (UI + CLI):
- [ ] Change bundle ID matches ticket/approval bundle
- [ ] No policy widening (egress/ingress broadening)
- [ ] Rollback plan attached and validated
- [ ] Customer notification configured (email/webhook)
- [ ] (optional) Attach ticket id or change request
- On approval: operator enters a 20-200 char justification.

State machine (high level):
requested -> human_approved -> applied -> archived
requested -> auto_approved -> applied -> archived
any -> rejected -> archived
applied -> post_check_failed -> rollback_initiated -> rolled_back

Auto-approve heuristics (experiment 1):
Candidate auto-approve only when ALL of the following are true:
- diff analyzer classifies change as low-risk (no open ports, no policy widening, small delta)
- operator is in trusted operator list (role-based + tenure > 90 days)
- change size under threshold (e.g., < 50 lines) and ticket id present
- customer opted into low-risk automation
If auto-approve triggers, artifact.approval_state=auto_approved and telemetry emits auto_approve=true with reason_code.

Experiment variants:
- Variant A: baseline manual human approvals (current).
- Variant B: auto-approve when diff analyzer + trusted operator + opt-in.
- Variant C: friction-reduced UI (pre-filled checklist + 1-click confirm).
Metrics to collect:
- approval_latency_p50/p95
- percent_auto_approved
- rollback_rate_within_24h
- evidence_completeness_score (audit checks pass %)
- operator_friction_score (short survey)
Stop conditions: run 6 weeks or until 1000 approval events per variant; abort auto-approve early if rollback_rate > 1%.

Observability queries (examples):
- list artifacts for tenant X between dates; filter by approval_state
- map artifact -> control_plane_request_id -> full diff status
- group rollbacks by operator_id and reason_code

Webhook / customer export (example payload):
{
  "artifact_id": "art_20260201_0a1b",
  "tenant": "acme-corp",
  "state": "human_approved",
  "signed_url": "https://s3.redwood/.../full-diff.tgz?sig=...",
  "operator": "emily.chen",
  "time": "2026-02-01T15:12:04Z"
}

Retention model (proposal):
- Artifact index (compact) stored in control-plane DB with configurable retention; default 7 years for regulated customers.
- Full diffs in encrypted blobstore; per-customer retention controls and eDiscovery export APIs.
- Signed artifacts must include metadata for chain-of-custody verification by third parties.

Fail-safes / rollback playbook:
- On post-deploy failure, system auto-creates rollback ticket and triggers rollback; operator must attest the rollback action and sign a rollback artifact.
- If signature validation fails on ingest, artifact marked suspect and security-on-call paged.

Infra implementation notes (minimal):
- DB schema additions: approval_state, artifact_id, diff_digest, operator_assertion fields on audit-index table.
- Sidecar service: idempotent artifact builder + signer (KMS), pushes compact artifact to index and emits telemetry.
- Keep artifact export paths attached to existing telemetry/storage pipelines; avoid duplicating event storage.

Open questions / edge cases to triage:
- canonicalization algorithm for diffs to ensure deterministic digests across clients?
- operator impersonation risk if accounts are shared (recommend enforcing MFA + operator_id rotation).
- batched changes spanning multiple steps: do we chain artifacts or create a parent artifact?
- EU retention semantics (GDPR + eDiscovery) and legal guidance.

Security + compliance minimums:
- Signatures produced via customer-managed KMS or Redwood KMS per customer preference.
- Signed URLs for full diffs with short TTL; artifacts exportable in bulk for audits.
- Admin revocation: admins can revoke operator keys and mark artifacts as revoked; revocations must themselves be auditable.

90-day rollout plan (high level):
- Week 1-3: implement sidecar + artifact index; run internal-only trials on staging.
- Week 4-6: pilot canary with 4-6 opt-in customers; collect baseline metrics.
- Week 7-12: run experiment variants across pilots; iterate heuristics and UI.
- Week 13: post-mortem, finalize PRD and compliance docs, prepare broader rollout.

Open tasks (short):
- [ ] Publish canonical artifact schema on Confluence (linked).
- [ ] Spec sidecar idempotency and retry semantics; add tests.
- [ ] Usability tests for 1-click approval UI and operator messaging.

Reviewer notes:
- This is intentionally pragmatic: ship an experiment and iterate. Please focus feedback on artifact shape, telemetry signals, and safety heuristics for auto-approve.

Owner / contact: Emily Chen <emily.chen@redwood.com>
